title: I got tired of managing my game's development through AI chats, so I built this
author: devtainer
selftext:
I'm making a game with AI coding tools, and tracking features, bugs, and follow-ups across chats was getting messy. I built this board to keep the development work in one place.



What I use it for:

\- One shared board for Codex and Claude Code; agents create, categorize, and update task cards.

\- Clear statuses: open, in progress, waiting for input, ready for review, and done.

\- Filters for status, priority, categories, and tags.

\- One-click task launch in Codex, without leaving the board.

\- Links from a task to its chat and back.

\- The latest recorded prompt and agent response inside each card.

\- Task history, recorded work sessions, a timeline, and activity charts.

\- Local storage; the tracker itself works offline.



I keep it open in a pinned Codex chat's browser panel, answer questions when a task needs me, and review the results before accepting them. How are you organizing AI-assisted work on your games?



If you're interested, you can try it here: \[GitHub\](https://github.com/AbramoMO/project-task-board). The README includes a setup prompt to paste into your coding agent. Free for individual use;
